cannot_claim: measured TE from one human ribo-seq dataset; condition-specific; still not causal
RPFdb processed CDS TE is used as a direct measured TE readout, not as a universal human translation-efficiency constant
the Ribo-seq and RNA-seq rawcount columns are retained as positive support measurements and are not claimed to reproduce RPFdb's internal normalization
gene-level Ensembl IDs are mapped to one longest-CDS ENSP representative; unmapped genes and non-positive measurements are discarded
id_mapping_method: RPFdb Ensembl gene IDs are stripped of version suffix and matched exactly to the gene:ENSG field in the existing FibonacciReality Homo sapiens Ensembl CDS headers; when multiple CDS records share one Ensembl gene, the longest CDS representative protein_id is emitted; all unmapped or non-positive genes are skipped.
source_kind: RPFdb processed CDS translation-efficiency table with matched Ribo-seq and RNA-seq rawcount support
study_ref: RPFdb processed Homo sapiens GSE56887, Wolfe et al. 2014 Nature, eIF4A-dependent oncogene translation in cancer
te_definition: direct positive RPFdb CDS translation-efficiency value from H.sapiens_GSE56887_TE_CDS.txt.gz, averaged across positive TE columns for each Ensembl gene; footprint and mRNA fields are mean positive rawcounts from the matched Ribo-seq and RNA-seq RPFdb rawcount tables for the same study and gene
